content: A friend asks what's the deal with the dog. Once a very long time ago, when I was living in Silicon Valley, I had a black lab named BonBon. She was a handful, for sure -- and I didn't know anything about training dogs, so she was also pretty wild. But she had the biggest heart and was totally devoted to me, and was pretty much my constant companion. Her joy in life was infectuous and memorable. Now I don't want to sound all gushy (go ahead) but BonBon the software which is named after BonBon the pup, gives me that feeling of joy too. I loved the web as much as I ever loved anything, because it blew open the doors on a really fucked up industry run by total children, whose first impulse was to destroy anything they could, even if it wasn't in their way. They did that to the web. But the web, via BonBon, says basically, you can do it. The courage of that little dog, BonBon, with the same name in two different contexts, reminds me that this is right, and it is working.
